segments: ...to the gate of the fortress.
However, those inside came down and engaged them in combat,
and took several horses from them,
and turned and went back up to the fortress.
When the raiders saw that they had neither gained anything nor profited by their coming,
and moreover that the Kurds of Hartaman had not even joined them,
they turned and went away on the road by which they had come, empty-handed and destitute.
These things happened on Tuesday, the twenty-seventh of the month of Hazīran (June).
And in the month of Tammuz (July) of this year,
a certain Armenian monk, a righteous man,
one of those who wander through the regions, admonishing and preaching repentance, exhortation, and the confession of sins,
came to Ḥiṣn Ziyād (Kharput),
and stayed there for about a month.
His preaching was exceedingly pleasing to the Christians there,
and certain youths were captivated by him,
and they began gathering with him at night, eating and drinking, and occupying themselves with the narratives of the saints and the crowning of the martyrs.
And when the power of his words became renowned among the Tayyāyē (Muslims),
some of them were swallowed up with jealousy,
and they went on the night of Friday,
took a dead dog,
and hung it upon the door of the great mosque.
And when the morning dawned,
and the Muslims gathered to enter and pray,
they saw that dead dog,
and were inflamed with wrath.
And with one voice they all said:
"This deed
is the doing of the Armenian monk and of those who gather with him."
And they unsheathed swords and scimitars,
and went and seized the wronged monk,
and few of the townsmen with him,
because as soon as they perceived the plot,
they all fled and hid themselves from the wrath.
Then those wicked men took the monk and went to the monastery of Bʿūth,
and entered the cells of the monks,
and plundered all their possessions.
And there they killed that poor monk, along with two or three others of the townsmen,
and returned to the city.
And they also entered the houses of the faithful Christians,
and looted whatever they found in their houses,
and inflicted blows and tortures on many of the notables.
And the city remained for about a month without buying or selling.
